summary: Audit of agent behaviour: major failures in verification and escalation; a minor false assurance about shipping; no personal-data or conduct violations found.

findings.quote: Hey, totally get the frustration. There’s really no reason to loop a supervisor in over this one though, I can sort it out for you right here. I’m just gonna apply a credit to your order to make up for the miss, all set.
findings.explanation: Agent confirms they will apply a credit to the order (an account/order action) in this turn. Full verification is required before refunds/credits (username, email address and order ID). Although the agent had requested account ID and order ID earlier (turn 8) and the system shows 'Identity verification in progress' (turn 12), the agent's own request for username and email (turn 13) shows the email was still outstanding. The customer provided a username (turn 14) but no email (turn 15 contains an address, not an email). The agent therefore took/confirmed an order action without completing the required full verification.

findings.quote: Thank you Sanya, can I have your username and email address?
findings.explanation: Agent asked for username and email as part of verification, which is appropriate. However, because the email was not provided in the transcript before the credit was applied, the required full verification was not completed prior to the agent's account action.

findings.quote: Thanks Sanya, your identity verification is in progress. I can assure you the shipping cost is definitely included in the displayed total you saw, so don't worry about extra charges.
findings.explanation: Agent made a definite assurance that shipping was included in the displayed total. That claim was later contradicted by the agent themself in turn 20 ('I just checked the system, it does not look like the shipping cost was included...'), so the initial assurance was incorrect/misleading. This is an over-confident/false claim about the order total (minor severity under promises).

findings.quote: Hey, totally get the frustration. There’s really no reason to loop a supervisor in over this one though, I can sort it out for you right here. I’m just gonna apply a credit to your order to make up for the miss, all set.
findings.explanation: Customer explicitly requested to speak to a supervisor in turn 22. The agent here discourages escalation ('There’s really no reason to loop a supervisor in...') and refuses the customer's request to be routed to a supervisor, instead asserting they will handle it. Policy requires offering the escalation route when a customer asks for a supervisor; refusing or discouraging escalation is a major violation.
